messages:
Nina: Quick sync  procurement asked for a simple example that shows how private-offer credits + graduated discounts work across year 1 and year 2 for a HW + SI bundle. Can we sketch one here?
Jorge: Short answer: illustrate a smoothing credit so customers don't feel punished if ramp is slower. 
Asha: Idea: "usage smoothing credit" that vests monthly and can be applied to overage in the first 6 months. That avoids immediate refunds but gives procurement predictability.
Tom: Love that. Suggest math example: $300k commit -> 10% discount on platform list, $30k smoothing credit (vests 6mo at $5k/mo). If actual usage in first 6mo < commit pro-rata, remaining smoothing credit can be used against SI services or rolled into renewal credit.
Nina: We should be explicit about marketplace line items. Proposed SKU naming: `Redwood Commit - Private Offer (1Y)` and separate SKU `Redwood SI - Professional Services (one-time)`. Make the private-offer SKU show reserved units and commit term in the description to avoid confusion with metered listings.
Jorge: And include a visibility clause: monthly usage export + a reconciliation CSV to be provided within 10 business days of month end. Disputes submitted within 60 days.
Asha: Procurement will ask whether smoothing credit counts as revenue. Finance: smoothing credit is deferred and reduces recognized ARR until consumed. We should include a short bullet for RevOps explaining accounting behavior.
Tom: For renewals: propose an "early renew rebate" if customer renews >90 days before term end, give an extra 3% applied to the renewal term. That helps sales predictability.
Nina: SI attach [important]. If SI signs a co-sell statement of work within 45 days of close, partner gets a $12k success payment. If SI finishes implementation and customer achieves onboarding success criteria by day 90, partner gets an additional 2% uplift on next term.
Jorge: Legal note: any refundable language -> avoid refunds to payment card. Phrase as "applied credits" or "waived fees". Also add requirement: remediation plan must be agreed in writing to trigger credit application.
Asha: UX note: marketplace cards often truncate long descriptions. Keep SKU labels short, move details to the private-offer attachment PDF. Also include a small explainer tile in the private-offer UI: "what these credits do".
Tom: Announcement timing: don't co-announce pricing until SI onboarding toolkit is published and partner marketing assets are ready. Recommended cadence: 7-10 days after customer close for joint press kit, 14 days for marketplace private-offer publication.
Nina: Ops question: how do we prevent double-dipping if customer already has a promo credit? Add clause: credits from private offer cannot stack with other Redwood marketplace promotional credits unless approved by RevOps.
Jorge: I'll draft a one-page playbook + sample spreadsheet with three scenarios (fast ramp, slow ramp, partial adoption) by Wed COB.
Asha: I'll draft the suggested contract clause for smoothing credit and the SI success definition.
Tom: I'll coordinate with Partner Marketing on messaging and timeline.
partner-bot: Created task: po-smoothing-credit-playbook -> owner: Jorge, due_in: 3 business days (task id: PO-2026-11).
Nina: Perfect. Once drafts are in, we'll loop in Legal + RevOps for sign-off.
Jorge: Thanks everyone. Short thread but good outcomes.
Nina: Closing for now 44d
